changes.current_line: Recover failed payments automatically with smart retries.
changes.change: Lead with the churn problem, not the mechanism: 'Win back the members who never meant to leave.' Back it in the first meetings with a recovery analysis of the prospect's own export of one month of failed renewals, showing which ones usually come back with a retry or an updated card ('Their file, not our average'). Early on, ask for the prospect's split between members who cancelled and members whose card failed.
changes.why: The buyer saw failed cards as members 'who never meant to leave' inside a board-level churn number, and the pitch that landed was failed payment recovery shown on their own renewals file, not a generic retry claim.

changes.change: Add a finance-facing proof pack for the controller or CFO, sent before the contract goes to finance: a take-away spreadsheet of recoverable revenue from their own failed renewals, plus a plain statement of our contract term and termination fees.
changes.why: The controller said nothing for two meetings, asked for the spreadsheet, sat on the paper for two weeks, and signed four days after the data session, and he asked about termination fees twice.

changes.current_line: Financial infrastructure to grow globally, in every currency.
changes.change: Stop opening with the global line for buyers whose footprint is not global, like this one with studios in the US and a handful in Canada. Open with the failed-renewal recovery analysis instead.
changes.why: The rep opened with the global slide and got 'Silence' from a customer with studios in the US and a handful in Canada.

changes.current_line: Online and in-store on one platform; the line between them has pretty much disappeared.
changes.change: For buyers whose front desk runs inside third-party studio software, stop leading with one-platform claims. Instead, position membership billing as a standalone win that does not depend on the front desk. Only make the in-store claim once we can show our reader live in their own software: 'Check a member in, sell a water bottle, same screen.'
changes.why: The unified commerce line was heard as 'is that the readers?', it pulled the conversation to hardware where we could only show a partner demo outside their setup, and the front desk stayed with the incumbent.
